author_or_org: Cheng Yang, Xuemeng Yang, Licheng Wen, Daocheng Fu, Jianbiao Mei, Rong Wu, Pinlong Cai, Yufan Shen, Nianchen Deng, Botian Shi, Yu Qiao, Haifeng Li

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Existing LLM agents are described as test-time static and unable to learn from experience, so they cannot accumulate knowledge or continuously improve on the job.
claims.quote: Existing LLM agents suffer from a critical limitation: they are test-time static and cannot learn from experience, lacking the ability to accumulate knowledge and continuously improve on the job.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: MUSE is an experience-driven, self-evolving agent framework centered on a hierarchical Memory Module that organizes experience and uses it to plan and execute long-horizon tasks across multiple applications.
claims.quote: To address this challenge, we propose MUSE, a novel agent framework that introduces an experience-driven, self-evolving system centered around a hierarchical Memory Module. MUSE organizes diverse levels of experience and leverages them to plan and execute long-horizon tasks across multiple applications.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: After each sub-task, MUSE autonomously reflects on its trajectory, converts the raw trajectory into structured experience, and integrates it back into the Memory Module.
claims.quote: After each sub-task execution, the agent autonomously reflects on its trajectory, converting the raw trajectory into structured experience and integrating it back into the Memory Module.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The MUSE mechanism lets the agent evolve beyond its static pretrained parameters, supporting continuous learning and self-evolution.
claims.quote: This mechanism enables the agent to evolve beyond its static pretrained parameters, fostering continuous learning and self-evolution.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: MUSE was evaluated on the long-horizon productivity benchmark TAC and achieved new state-of-the-art performance by a significant margin using only a lightweight Gemini-2.5 Flash model.
claims.quote: We evaluate MUSE on the long-horizon productivity benchmark TAC. It achieves new SOTA performance by a significant margin using only a lightweight Gemini-2.5 Flash model.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Experiments indicate that as MUSE autonomously accumulates experience, its task completion improves and it shows robust continuous learning and self-evolution.
claims.quote: Sufficient Experiments demonstrate that as the agent autonomously accumulates experience, it exhibits increasingly superior task completion capabilities, as well as robust continuous learning and self-evolution capabilities.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: MUSE's accumulated experience shows generalization properties that enable zero-shot improvement on new tasks.
claims.quote: Moreover, the accumulated experience from MUSE exhibits strong generalization properties, enabling zero-shot improvement on new tasks.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The paper positions MUSE as establishing a new paradigm for AI agents capable of real-world productivity task automation.
claims.quote: MUSE establishes a new paradigm for AI agents capable of real-world productivity task automation.
